OBITUARY REFERENCE 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, I refer with profound sorrow 
to the tragic and untimely demise of Shri G.M.C. Balayogi, Speaker, 
Lok Sabha, on the 3 rd March, 2002 in a helicopter crash in Kaikalur, 
West Godavari District, Andhra Pradesh, at the age of 51. A promising 
career has, thus, been cut short at the unkind hands of destiny. 
Born in October 1951 at Yedurulanka in East Godavari District 
of Andhra Pradesh, Shri Balayogi wa s associated with several social 
and cultural organisations and took special interest in the upliftment of 
the poor and the downtrodden sections of the society.. 
Shri Balayogi started his career with the Vice-Chairmanship of 
the Cooperative Town Bank of Kakinada in 1986. Thereafter, he 
became Chairman, Zila Praja Parishad, East Godavari District, in 
1987, in which post he continued till 1991. He was elected as a 
Member of the Tenth Lok Sabha in 1991. He was elected to the 
Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assemb ly in 1996 and remained as its 
Member till 1998. He also served as the Minister of Higher Education 
in the Andhra Pradesh Government and took the initiative in 
streamlining and reforming the educational system. In 1998, he was 
again elected as a Member of the Twelfth Lok Sabha and was elected 
as the Speaker, Lok Sabha, in March, 1998. In 1999, he was re-
elected to the Thirteenth Lok Sabha for the third time and was elected 
as the Speaker of the Lok Sabha for the second time in October, 1999 
and continued to hold office till his death. 
In his capacity as Speaker, he was Chairman of the Business 
Advisory Committee, Rules Committee. General Purposes Committee 
of the Lok Sabha and Presiding Officer of the Legislative Bodies in 
India. He was also President of the Indian Parliamentary Group, the 
National Group of Inter-Parliamentary Union and the India Branch of 
the Commonwealth Parliamentary Association. 

RAJYA SABHA [4 March, 2002] 
He  led the  Indian  Parliamentary Delegations to the  Ninety-
ninth, Hundredth and Hundred-and -first Inter-Parliamentary Union 
Conferences and the Forty-fourth and Forty-fifth Commonwealth 
Parliamentary Conferences. He also led several Parliamentary 
Delegations to various countries. 
He adorned the high office of the Speaker at a young age and 
conducted the proceedings of the Lok Sabha smoothly and efficiently. 
As the Presiding Officer of the House, he ensured that all sections of 
the House got equal opportunity to participate in the proceedings of 
the House in a fair and orderly manner. He stood for norms and 
ethical values. At his initiative, in a Conference of the Chief Ministers, 
Presiding Officers and Leaders of various political parties in 
Parliament and State Legislatures, a Code of Conduct to be observed 
by Members of Parliament and State Legislatures was adopted. Soft 
spoken and mild mannered, he endeared himself to one and all, and 
showed firmness, when needed. 
In the passing away of Shri G.M.C. Balayogi, the country has 
lost a young and dynamic parliamentarian. 
I request Members to rise in their places and observe silence as 
a mark of respect to the memory of the departed. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute.) 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Secr etary-General will convey to the 
members of the bereaved family our sense of profound sorrow and 
deep sympathy, 
As a mark of respect to the memory of Shri G.M.C. Balayogi, 
Speaker, Lok Sabha, the House stands adjourned till 11.00 a.m. on 
Thursday, the 7th March, 2002. 
The House then adjourned at five minutes past eleven of the clock, 
till eleven of the clock on Thursday, the 7th March, 2002.
